channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: How ‘AI-Pilled’ Companies Are Rewriting the Startup Playbook
item.description: AI isn’t just changing what startups build, it’s changing how the companies themselves operate. Floodgate co-founder and Partner Ann Miura-Ko explains her thesis around the “AI-pilled organization,” where agents are deployed across engineering, sales, marketing, and strategy to dramatically accelerate how companies learn and execute. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Data Center Demand Isn’t Slowing: Southern CEO
item.description: As the AI boom is driving one of the biggest data center buildouts in history, Southern Company CEO Chris Womack discusses the utility’s growing pipeline of data center projects, its 25-year agreement supporting OpenAI’s planned Georgia expansion, and why he says hyperscalers can bear the cost of new infrastructure while putting downward pressure on electricity rates for existing customers. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Settlement Sets Blueprint for TikTok, YouTube
item.description: Meta has agreed to pay up to $18 billion over ten years and adopt new protections for teenage users as part of a landmark settlement with states over its social media platforms. The company was sued by 29 state attorneys general, including West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey, who says the deal provides a “blueprint” for pursuing TikTok, YouTube, and other platforms. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Holders to Focus on AI Data, Mizuho's Rakesh Says
item.description: Nvidia Corp.'s outlook for artificial intelligence spending and revenue will be the focus for investors and analysts in Wednesday's earnings results, according to Mizuho Securities analyst Vijay Rakesh. He speaks with Dani Burger and Yahaira Anand on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Agrees to Settle Lawsuit Over Social Media Claims
item.description: Meta has agreed to pay up to $16.7 billion to resolve the lawsuit at the center of the trial in Oakland and as part of the settlement, will also put more safeguards in place for users between 13 and 17 years old. Ed Ludlow explains (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Earnings Live: Updates on Q2 2026 Results From AI Chipmaker
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Stocks Stall as Wall Street Awaits Nvidia | Open Interest 8/26/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks waver as traders hold back on risk ahead of Nvidia earnings and fresh signals on the durability of the AI trade. US consumer spending stalls in July while the Fed's preferred inflation gauge rises as expected, bolstering the case for rates to stay on hold. Meta agrees to pay $16.7 billion to settle a landmark case over teens’ addiction to Facebook and Instagram. Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji and Altruist CEO Jason Wenk explain why they decided to combine assets. Plus, CityPickle Co-CEO Mary Cannon on the explosive growth of pickleball. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Up to Half of Planned US Data Centers May Face Delays, Kimmeridge Says
item.description: As many as half of the proposed data centers in the US are at risk of delays or cancellations because of growing political backlash and the complexities of building physical assets, according to investment firm Kimmeridge Energy Management Co.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Liao

item.title: Anthropic to Pay Nscale $45 Billion for AI Computing Power
item.description: Anthropic PBC has agreed to spend $45 billion to rent AI cloud computing power from Nscale’s flagship data center development in West Virginia, the latest move in an effort to secure capacity for its expanding business in advance of going public.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Meta, States Agree To Settle Teen Social Media Case
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. said it agreed to pay up to $18 billion in landmark settlements to resolve allegations from multiple US states that the company deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to encourage compulsive use among young users. Matthew Schettenhelm, Bloomberg Intelligence Media Litigation Analyst joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple to Ship 10 Million Foldable iPhones in Year One, IDC Says
item.description: Apple Inc.’s anticipated foldable iPhone will rescue that segment of the smartphone market from decline and deliver more than 10 million shipments in its first year, researcher IDC predicts.
item.dc:creator: Vlad Savov

item.title: Five Takeaways From Bill Gates’ Essay on AI’s Potential Risks
item.description: Bill Gates waded into the debate over artificial intelligence, urging tech companies and regulators to get serious now about the risks the powerful technology poses to humanity.
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley

item.title: Apple to Hold Sept. 9 Foldable iPhone Launch to Start Ternus Era
item.description: Apple Inc. will hold its biggest product introduction of the year on Sept. 9, kicking off the tenure of new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Lockheed’s Pricey F-35 Sees 10% Cost Jump for Needed Upgrades
item.description: The cost of the Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35 program — already the most expensive in US history — has risen by about $51 billion, or about 10%, since late 2023 because of software, readiness, spare parts and engine power improvements.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Read How Meta Plans to Curb Kids’ Use of Facebook and Instagram
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. agreed to implement a raft of restrictions for teens on its Facebook and Instagram apps as part of a multibillion-dollar settlement with multiple US states on Wednesday. The landmark agreement requires the company to put new guardrails on Facebook and Instagram, including limits on how much time youths can spend scrolling and preventing them from switching off certain safety settings without parental consent.
item.dc:creator: Molly Schuetz

item.title: Meta Agrees to $16.7 Billion Settlement in Social Media Case
item.description: Meta Platforms has reached a $16.7 billion settlement in a high-profile case concerning harm caused to teens through its social media platforms. The settlement amount is significantly lower than Meta's worst-case scenario estimate of $1.4 trillion, which represented the maximum potential penalties if all accusations had been upheld at their severest levels. Ed Ludlow reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Says It Will Pay Up to $18 Billion Over Social Media Claims
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. said it agreed to pay up to $18 billion in landmark settlements to resolve allegations from multiple US states that the company deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to encourage compulsive use among young users.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Gates Criticizes Tech Companies for Downplaying AI’s Risks
item.description: Bill Gates says tech companies are minimizing the perils artificial intelligence poses to humanity.
item.dc:creator: Robin Ajello and Matt Day

item.title: China’s Z.ai Made Ox Alpha Stealth Model, Rivaling DeepSeek
item.description: The new artificial intelligence model that’s swept to the top of online usage charts with high performance at zero cost was created by China’s Z.AI Co., also known as Zhipu.
item.dc:creator: Luz Ding

item.title: McGraw Hill CEO Philip Moyer on AI’s Impact in Education
item.description: Philip Moyer, CEO of McGraw Hill, spoke about the evolving role of AI in education during the back-to-school period. He emphasized that McGraw Hill, a longstanding education company, now serves both traditional and digital learning needs globally, with around 100 million curriculum licenses and 7.5 million active users across their AI-powered solutions. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
